186	out_c2="$(
187	  CLAUDE_PROJECT_ROOT="${ROOT}" LEADV2_PROJECT_ROOT="${ROOT}" \
188	  LEADV2_DISPATCH_CACHE_DIR="${CACHE_DIR}" \
189	  LEADV2_DISPATCH_SUBSESSION_BIN="${FAKE_SUBSESSION}" \
190	  LEADV2_DISPATCH_ARCHITECT_GATE=0 \
191	  LEADV2_DISPATCH_E2E_GATE=0 LEADV2_DISPATCH_REVIEW_GATE=0 \
192	  LEADV2_JOURNAL_BIN=/bin/true \
193	  LEADV2_ROUTER_V2=0 \

195	  LEADV2_LANE_SHAPE=off \

197	)"
198	rc_c2=$?
199	row_c2="$(tail -1 "${LEDGER_FILE}" 2>/dev/null)"
200	if [[ "${rc_c2}" -eq 0 ]] && grep -q '"task_id":""' <<<"${row_c2}"; then
201	  pass "C2: no --task-id, mission has no H1 -> reserve row task_id is empty (no invented name)"
202	else
203	  fail "C2: no --task-id, mission has no H1 -> reserve row task_id is empty (got rc=${rc_c2}, row: ${row_c2}, out: ${out_c2})"
204	fi
205	
206	# C3: --task-id PRESENT and mission has an H1 -> reserve row task_id == the --task-id
207	# (rule 1 wins; guards against this fix hijacking the fanout path, which always binds
208	# --task-id and must never have it overridden by mission prose).
209	c3_mission_file="${TMPDIR_ROOT}/c3-mission.md"
210	cat > "${c3_mission_file}" <<EOF
211	# N7F-C3-WRONG-NAME — must NOT win over the bound --task-id
212	body text, dispatch-ledger-task-id c3 $$ $(date +%s 2>/dev/null || echo 0)
213	EOF
214	C3_TASK_ID="N7F-C3-BOUND-ID"
215	out_c3="$(
216	  CLAUDE_PROJECT_ROOT="${ROOT}" LEADV2_PROJECT_ROOT="${ROOT}" \
217	  LEADV2_DISPATCH_CACHE_DIR="${CACHE_DIR}" \
218	  LEADV2_DISPATCH_SUBSESSION_BIN="${FAKE_SUBSESSION}" \
219	  LEADV2_DISPATCH_ARCHITECT_GATE=0 \
220	  LEADV2_DISPATCH_E2E_GATE=0 LEADV2_DISPATCH_REVIEW_GATE=0 \
221	  LEADV2_JOURNAL_BIN=/bin/true \
222	  LEADV2_ROUTER_V2=0 \
223	  LEADV2_EXCLUDED_ARMS="__none__" \
224	  LEADV2_LANE_SHAPE=off \
225	  "${DISPATCH_SH}" "@${c3_mission_file}" --protected --spawn --kind docs --task-id "${C3_TASK_ID}" 2>&1
226	)"
227	rc_c3=$?
228	row_c3="$(tail -1 "${LEDGER_FILE}" 2>/dev/null)"
229	if [[ "${rc_c3}" -eq 0 ]] && grep -q "\"task_id\":\"${C3_TASK_ID}\"" <<<"${row_c3}"; then
230	  pass "C3: --task-id AND mission-H1 both present -> reserve row task_id == bound --task-id (rule 1 wins)"
231	else
232	  fail "C3: --task-id AND mission-H1 both present -> reserve row task_id == bound --task-id (got rc=${rc_c3}, row: ${row_c3}, out: ${out_c3})"
233	fi
234	
235	# C4/C5 isolate the terminal ledger file the SAME way test-t-core-dispatch-ledger.sh
236	# does (LEADV2_DISPATCH_TERMINAL_LEDGER_FILE override) rather than re-deriving
237	# dispatch_terminal_ledger_file()'s CACHE_BASE fallback path here -- that fn tries
238	# leadv2-state-path.sh FIRST, which (unlike dispatch-code.sh's own simpler

242	TERMINAL_LEDGER_FILE="${TMPDIR_ROOT}/terminal-ledger.jsonl"
243	
244	# C4: leadv2-dispatch-ledger.sh write-terminal driven directly with a display-name 7th
245	# arg and an EMPTY founder -- covers the class=product terminal writer (dispatch-
246	# product-close.sh) without spawning a real close gate. Expect: task_id from the
247	# display name, founder_task_id stays empty.
248	C4_SIG8="c4sig888"
249	C4_NAME="N7F-C4-Display"
250	LEADV2_DISPATCH_TERMINAL_LEDGER_FILE="${TERMINAL_LEDGER_FILE}" PROJECT_ROOT="${ROOT}" \
251	  LEADV2_JOURNAL_BIN=/bin/true \
252	  bash "${LEDGER_SH}" write-terminal "${C4_SIG8}" "" landed test_cause "" "attempt-c4" "${C4_NAME}" >/dev/null 2>&1
253	row_c4="$(grep -F "\"task_sig\":\"${C4_SIG8}\"" "${TERMINAL_LEDGER_FILE}" 2>/dev/null | tail -1)"
254	if grep -q "\"task_id\":\"${C4_NAME}\"" <<<"${row_c4}" && grep -q '"founder_task_id":""' <<<"${row_c4}"; then
255	  pass "C4: write-terminal with empty founder + display-name 7th arg -> task_id from display name, founder_task_id empty"
256	else
257	  fail "C4: write-terminal with empty founder + display-name 7th arg (got row: ${row_c4})"
258	fi
259	
260	# C5: write-terminal with 6 args (no display name) -> task_id falls back to founder
261	# (back-compat: a pre-N7F-LANE-NAME caller's output is byte-identical).
262	C5_SIG8="c5sig888"
263	C5_FOUNDER="N7F-C5-Founder"
264	LEADV2_DISPATCH_TERMINAL_LEDGER_FILE="${TERMINAL_LEDGER_FILE}" PROJECT_ROOT="${ROOT}" \
265	  LEADV2_JOURNAL_BIN=/bin/true \
266	  bash "${LEDGER_SH}" write-terminal "${C5_SIG8}" "${C5_FOUNDER}" landed test_cause "" "attempt-c5" >/dev/null 2>&1
267	row_c5="$(grep -F "\"task_sig\":\"${C5_SIG8}\"" "${TERMINAL_LEDGER_FILE}" 2>/dev/null | tail -1)"
268	if grep -q "\"task_id\":\"${C5_FOUNDER}\"" <<<"${row_c5}"; then
269	  pass "C5: write-terminal with 6 args (no display name) -> task_id falls back to founder (back-compat)"
270	else
271	  fail "C5: write-terminal with 6 args (no display name) -> task_id falls back to founder (got row: ${row_c5})"
272	fi
273	
274	# ── N1B-ARM-COOLDOWN-HARDEN F4: identity vs display-label collision ───────────
275	# Finding 4: a no-`--task-id` mission headed `# OPS-42 — cleanup` used to land
276	# the H1 name-token "OPS-42" in the identity field, which the status reader then
277	# resolved against tasks.yaml -> rendered an UNRELATED record's title. After F4
278	# the label lives in lane_label (rendered verbatim, never looked up), so the row
279	# shows "OPS-42", not "Totally unrelated record".
280	RENDER_SH="${SCRIPTS_DIR}/leadv2-status-surface.sh"
281	F4_REPO="$(printf '%s' "$(basename "${ROOT}")" | tr -cd 'A-Za-z0-9._-')"
282	# render NOW ~= the reserve moment so the freshly-reserved row is within the
283	# freshness window (a dead handle at +166 days is age-dropped and never reaches
284	# resolve_name, which would make this test assert against nothing).
285	F4_NOW="$(date +%s 2>/dev/null || echo 1800000000)"
286	
287	# tasks.yaml fixture: an OPS-42 id that is NOT this mission.
288	F4_TASKS="${TMPDIR_ROOT}/f4-tasks.yaml"
289	cat > "${F4_TASKS}" <<'YAML'
290	meta: {}
291	tasks:
292	  - id: OPS-42
293	    title: Totally unrelated record
294	YAML
295	
296	# render the worker rows for one isolated ledger; echo the NAME (field 1) of the
297	# single data row. empty STATE_DIR (no active.yaml) -> reserve row renders as a
298	# worker row, name = resolve_name(task_id, lane_label, ...).
299	_f4_render_name() {  # <ledger_dir> <state_dir> <runs_root>
300	  LEADV2_STATUS_STATE_DIR="$2" \
301	  LEADV2_STATUS_LEDGER_DIR="$1" \
302	  LEADV2_STATUS_RUNS_ROOT="$3" \
303	  LEADV2_STATUS_REPO="${F4_REPO}" \
304	  LEADV2_STATUS_REPO_ROOT="${ROOT}" \
305	  LEADV2_STATUS_NOW="${F4_NOW}" \
306	  LEADV2_STATUS_TASKS_YAML="${F4_TASKS}" \
307	  bash "${RENDER_SH}" 2>/dev/null | awk '$NF ~ /^[0-9a-f]{6,}$/ {sub(/^ +/,""); sub(/ +(worker|lane) .*/,""); print; exit}'
308	}
309	
310	# F4: NO --task-id, mission H1 `# OPS-42 — cleanup` -> renders "OPS-42" (the
311	# label verbatim), NOT "Totally unrelated record" (the tasks.yaml title).
312	F4A_CACHE="${TMPDIR_ROOT}/f4a-cache"; F4A_LDIR="${F4A_CACHE}/dispatch-ledger"
313	F4A_STATE="${TMPDIR_ROOT}/f4a-state"; F4A_RUNS="${TMPDIR_ROOT}/f4a-runs"
314	mkdir -p "${F4A_LDIR}" "${F4A_STATE}" "${F4A_RUNS}"
315	# an empty-but-readable active.yaml keeps the renderer on its normal row path
316	# (a missing active.yaml takes the warn branch and suppresses the worker row).
317	printf 'meta: {}\nsessions: []\n' > "${F4A_STATE}/active.yaml"
318	f4a_mission="${TMPDIR_ROOT}/f4a-mission.md"
319	cat > "${f4a_mission}" <<EOF
320	# OPS-42 — cleanup, N1B-F4 no-task-id $$ $(date +%s 2>/dev/null || echo 0)
321	body: display label must not collide with the tasks.yaml OPS-42 identity
322	EOF
323	LEADV2_DISPATCH_CACHE_DIR="${F4A_CACHE}" \
324	  CLAUDE_PROJECT_ROOT="${ROOT}" LEADV2_PROJECT_ROOT="${ROOT}" \
325	  LEADV2_DISPATCH_SUBSESSION_BIN="${FAKE_SUBSESSION}" \
326	  LEADV2_DISPATCH_ARCHITECT_GATE=0 \
327	  LEADV2_DISPATCH_E2E_GATE=0 LEADV2_DISPATCH_REVIEW_GATE=0 \
328	  LEADV2_JOURNAL_BIN=/bin/true LEADV2_ROUTER_V2=0 \
329	  LEADV2_EXCLUDED_ARMS="__none__" LEADV2_LANE_SHAPE=off \
330	  "${DISPATCH_SH}" "@${f4a_mission}" --protected --spawn --kind docs >/dev/null 2>&1
331	f4a_name="$(_f4_render_name "${F4A_LDIR}" "${F4A_STATE}" "${F4A_RUNS}")"
332	if [[ "${f4a_name}" == "OPS-42" ]]; then
333	  pass "F4: no --task-id, mission H1 `# OPS-42 — cleanup` -> renders OPS-42 (not the tasks.yaml title)"
334	else
335	  fail "F4: no --task-id collision (got name=[${f4a_name}], want OPS-42)"
336	fi
337	
338	# F4b: WITH --task-id OPS-42 + same fixture -> renders the tasks.yaml title
339	# (the identity lookup is PRESERVED; this guards against the fix over-reaching
340	# and breaking the bound-identity path).
341	F4B_CACHE="${TMPDIR_ROOT}/f4b-cache"; F4B_LDIR="${F4B_CACHE}/dispatch-ledger"
342	F4B_STATE="${TMPDIR_ROOT}/f4b-state"; F4B_RUNS="${TMPDIR_ROOT}/f4b-runs"
343	mkdir -p "${F4B_LDIR}" "${F4B_STATE}" "${F4B_RUNS}"
344	printf 'meta: {}\nsessions: []\n' > "${F4B_STATE}/active.yaml"
345	f4b_mission="${TMPDIR_ROOT}/f4b-mission.md"
346	cat > "${f4b_mission}" <<EOF
347	# OPS-42 — cleanup, N1B-F4b with-task-id $$ $(date +%s 2>/dev/null || echo 0)
348	body: bound --task-id OPS-42 must still resolve via tasks.yaml
349	EOF
350	LEADV2_DISPATCH_CACHE_DIR="${F4B_CACHE}" \
351	  CLAUDE_PROJECT_ROOT="${ROOT}" LEADV2_PROJECT_ROOT="${ROOT}" \
352	  LEADV2_DISPATCH_SUBSESSION_BIN="${FAKE_SUBSESSION}" \
353	  LEADV2_DISPATCH_ARCHITECT_GATE=0 \
354	  LEADV2_DISPATCH_E2E_GATE=0 LEADV2_DISPATCH_REVIEW_GATE=0 \
355	  LEADV2_JOURNAL_BIN=/bin/true LEADV2_ROUTER_V2=0 \
356	  LEADV2_EXCLUDED_ARMS="__none__" LEADV2_LANE_SHAPE=off \
357	  "${DISPATCH_SH}" "@${f4b_mission}" --protected --spawn --kind docs --task-id OPS-42 >/dev/null 2>&1
358	f4b_name="$(_f4_render_name "${F4B_LDIR}" "${F4B_STATE}" "${F4B_RUNS}")"
359	if [[ "${f4b_name}" == "Totally unrelated record" ]]; then
360	  pass "F4b: --task-id OPS-42 -> renders the tasks.yaml title (identity lookup preserved)"
361	else
362	  fail "F4b: identity lookup (got name=[${f4b_name}], want 'Totally unrelated record')"
363	fi
364	
365	printf '[TEST] === %s passed, %s failed ===\n' "${PASS}" "${FAIL}"
366	[[ "${FAIL}" -eq 0 ]]

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# tests/test-dispatch-ledger-task-id.sh — SWIFTBAR-LIVE-01 round 2 (§2.4) writer regression.
#
# THE BUG: dispatch_reserve() called _dispatch_append_pending_locked with only 6 of its
# 8 positional args, so every pending-ledger row was written with task_id="" and
# mission_path="" -- even when the caller was invoked with --task-id N4-TESTRUNNER-FALSE-RED.
# The status surface then had nothing to name the lane by and fell back to scraping the
# mission's prose first line, rendering things like "You are implementing task
# dispatch-14b3b worker confirmed" as a lane's NAME.
#
# THIS TEST drives the REAL dispatch-code.sh (never a hand-reimplemented copy of the
# ledger-write logic) with a bound --task-id, same hermetic-fixture discipline as
# test-dispatch-duplicate-caller-race.sh / test-leadv2-dispatch-outcome-ledger.sh, and
# asserts the PENDING ledger row (the one leadv2-status-surface.sh reads for worker rows)
# carries a non-empty task_id equal to what was passed on the command line.
#
# Run: bash plugins/leadv2/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-ledger-task-id.sh

set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
SCRIPTS_DIR="$(cd "${SCRIPT_DIR}/.." && pwd)"
DISPATCH_SH="${SCRIPTS_DIR}/leadv2-dispatch-code.sh"
source "${SCRIPTS_DIR}/leadv2-temp.sh"

PASS=0; FAIL=0
pass() { PASS=$((PASS + 1)); printf '[TEST] PASS: %s\n' "$1"; }
fail() { FAIL=$((FAIL + 1)); printf '[TEST] FAIL: %s\n' "$1"; }

if bash -n "${DISPATCH_SH}" 2>/dev/null; then
  pass "bash -n leadv2-dispatch-code.sh"
else
  fail "bash -n leadv2-dispatch-code.sh"
fi
if bash -n "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}" 2>/dev/null; then
  pass "bash -n $(basename "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")"
else
  fail "bash -n $(basename "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")"
fi

RUN_ID="dispatch-ledger-task-id-$$-$(date +%s 2>/dev/null || echo 0)"
TMPDIR_ROOT="$(lv2_mktemp_dir "${RUN_ID}")"
ROOT="${TMPDIR_ROOT}/repo"
CACHE_DIR="${TMPDIR_ROOT}/cache"
FAKE_SUBSESSION="${TMPDIR_ROOT}/fake-claude-subsession.sh"
trap 'rm -rf "$TMPDIR_ROOT"' EXIT

mkdir -p "${ROOT}/.claude/ref" "${ROOT}/docs/leadv2/.bus-offsets" "${ROOT}/platform"
( cd "${ROOT}" && git init -q && git config user.email test@example.com && git config user.name test \
  && printf 'seed\n' > seed.txt && git add seed.txt && git commit -qm seed )

cat > "${ROOT}/.claude/ref/leadv2-routing.yaml" <<'YAML'
router:
  glm_policy:
    sonnet_exceptions:
      - id: safety_gate_publish_payments
    opus_only_mission_kinds: []
    codex_fitting_mission_kinds: []
    codex_default_tier: standard
YAML

# Same fake launcher shape as the other dispatch-code tests: spawns a real, short-lived
# OS process and prints its PID in the exact shape spawn_worker's sonnet-arm parser expects.
cat > "${FAKE_SUBSESSION}" <<'EOF'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -uo pipefail
nohup sleep 0.3 >/dev/null 2>&1 &
pid=$!
disown
printf 'PID=%s LABEL=fake-lane SESSION_ID=fake-session\n' "${pid}"
exit 0
EOF
chmod +x "${FAKE_SUBSESSION}"

TASK_ID="N4-TESTRUNNER-FALSE-RED"
mission="docs-only: dispatch-ledger-task-id $$ $(date +%s)"

out="$(
  CLAUDE_PROJECT_ROOT="${ROOT}" LEADV2_PROJECT_ROOT="${ROOT}" \
  LEADV2_DISPATCH_CACHE_DIR="${CACHE_DIR}" \
  LEADV2_DISPATCH_SUBSESSION_BIN="${FAKE_SUBSESSION}" \
  LEADV2_DISPATCH_ARCHITECT_GATE=0 \
  LEADV2_DISPATCH_E2E_GATE=0 LEADV2_DISPATCH_REVIEW_GATE=0 \
  LEADV2_JOURNAL_BIN=/bin/true \
  LEADV2_ROUTER_V2=0 \
  LEADV2_EXCLUDED_ARMS="__none__" \
  LEADV2_LANE_SHAPE=off \
  "${DISPATCH_SH}" "${mission}" --protected --spawn --task-id "${TASK_ID}" 2>&1
)"
rc=$?

if [[ "${rc}" -eq 0 ]]; then
  pass "dispatch with --task-id exits 0"
else
  fail "dispatch with --task-id exits 0 (got rc=${rc}, out=${out})"
fi

repo_base="$(basename "${ROOT}")"
repo_slug="$(printf '%s' "${repo_base}" | tr -cd 'A-Za-z0-9._-')"
LEDGER_FILE="${CACHE_DIR}/dispatch-ledger/${repo_slug}.jsonl"

if [[ -f "${LEDGER_FILE}" ]]; then
  pass "pending dispatch ledger file exists"
else
  fail "pending dispatch ledger file exists (expected ${LEDGER_FILE}; dir contents: $(ls -la "${CACHE_DIR}/dispatch-ledger" 2>&1))"
fi

row="$(tail -1 "${LEDGER_FILE}" 2>/dev/null)"

if grep -q "\"task_id\":\"${TASK_ID}\"" <<<"${row}"; then
  pass "ledger row's task_id equals the bound --task-id (${TASK_ID})"
else
  fail "ledger row's task_id equals the bound --task-id (got row: ${row})"
fi

if grep -q '"mission_path":""' <<<"${row}"; then
  # this dispatch passed the mission inline (not via @file), so an empty
  # mission_path is the correct, honest value here -- the writer link
  # (dispatch_reserve receiving DISPATCH_MISSION_PATH) is proven by task_id
  # above, which travels the identical code path.
  pass "ledger row's mission_path is empty for an inline (non-@file) mission, as expected"
else
  fail "ledger row's mission_path unexpected for an inline mission (got row: ${row})"
fi

# ── N7F-LANE-NAME extension ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#
# Why the six cases above never caught the live bug: N-7f's investigation found every
# real founder dispatch (the fanout path aside) runs WITHOUT --task-id, yet all six
# assertions above ALWAYS pass --task-id "${TASK_ID}" -- so this file exercised the one
# input shape (bound identity) that the live path never supplies, and its mission is a
# bare inline string with no H1, so even a mission-scrape fallback would have nothing to
# find. Concretely, three blindness properties, all present at once in the original
# suite:
#   1. it always passes --task-id -- the one input the live caller omits;
#   2. its mission is inline (`docs-only: ...`), never `class=product`, so the
#      prepass/act-two close-gate half of the writer chain is never reached;
#   3. it asserts only the pending/reserve row, never a terminal row -- and for a
#      product lane the terminal row is written by a DIFFERENT process
#      (leadv2-dispatch-product-close.sh), not dispatch-code.sh itself.
# C1-C3 close blindness #1 (drive the real --task-id-absent shape, with and without a
# mission H1). C4-C5 close blindness #3 (drive leadv2-dispatch-ledger.sh write-terminal
# directly, the product-lane terminal writer, without spawning a real close gate).

LEDGER_SH="${SCRIPTS_DIR}/leadv2-dispatch-ledger.sh"

# C1: @file mission WITH an H1 heading, NO --task-id. N1B F4 changed the schema:
# the H1 name-token is now a DISPLAY label (lane_label), NOT an identity. So the
# reserve row carries task_id="" (no founder identity bound) AND
# lane_label="N7F-C1" (the prose-derived display name). Before F4 the label went
# into task_id and collided with tasks.yaml identities -- exactly Finding 4.
c1_mission_file="${TMPDIR_ROOT}/c1-mission.md"
cat > "${c1_mission_file}" <<EOF
# N7F-C1 — case one heading, dispatch-ledger-task-id $$ $(date +%s 2>/dev/null || echo 0)
body text, deliberately no --task-id on this dispatch
EOF

out_c1="$(
  CLAUDE_PROJECT_ROOT="${ROOT}" LEADV2_PROJECT_ROOT="${ROOT}" \
  LEADV2_DISPATCH_CACHE_DIR="${CACHE_DIR}" \
  LEADV2_DISPATCH_SUBSESSION_BIN="${FAKE_SUBSESSION}" \
  LEADV2_DISPATCH_ARCHITECT_GATE=0 \
  LEADV2_DISPATCH_E2E_GATE=0 LEADV2_DISPATCH_REVIEW_GATE=0 \
  LEADV2_JOURNAL_BIN=/bin/true \
  LEADV2_ROUTER_V2=0 \
  LEADV2_EXCLUDED_ARMS="__none__" \
  LEADV2_LANE_SHAPE=off \
  "${DISPATCH_SH}" "@${c1_mission_file}" --protected --spawn --kind docs 2>&1
)"
rc_c1=$?
row_c1="$(tail -1 "${LEDGER_FILE}" 2>/dev/null)"
if [[ "${rc_c1}" -eq 0 ]] && grep -q '"task_id":""' <<<"${row_c1}"; then
  pass "C1: no --task-id -> reserve row task_id is EMPTY (identity absent, not the H1)"
else
  fail "C1: no --task-id -> task_id empty (got rc=${rc_c1}, row: ${row_c1})"
fi
if [[ "${rc_c1}" -eq 0 ]] && grep -q '"lane_label":"N7F-C1"' <<<"${row_c1}"; then
  pass "C1: no --task-id, mission has H1 -> reserve row lane_label == H1 name-token (N7F-C1)"
else
  fail "C1: no --task-id, mission has H1 -> lane_label == H1 name-token (got row: ${row_c1})"
fi

# C2: mission with NO H1, NO --task-id -> reserve row task_id is empty (rule 3: no
# invented name -- never a hash, filename, or prose fragment).
c2_mission="plain mission body, no heading line, dispatch-ledger-task-id c2 $$ $(date +%s 2>/dev/null || echo 0)"
out_c2="$(
  CLAUDE_PROJECT_ROOT="${ROOT}" LEADV2_PROJECT_ROOT="${ROOT}" \
  LEADV2_DISPATCH_CACHE_DIR="${CACHE_DIR}" \
  LEADV2_DISPATCH_SUBSESSION_BIN="${FAKE_SUBSESSION}" \
  LEADV2_DISPATCH_ARCHITECT_GATE=0 \
  LEADV2_DISPATCH_E2E_GATE=0 LEADV2_DISPATCH_REVIEW_GATE=0 \
  LEADV2_JOURNAL_BIN=/bin/true \
  LEADV2_ROUTER_V2=0 \
  LEADV2_EXCLUDED_ARMS="__none__" \
  LEADV2_LANE_SHAPE=off \
  "${DISPATCH_SH}" "${c2_mission}" --protected --spawn --kind docs 2>&1
)"
rc_c2=$?
row_c2="$(tail -1 "${LEDGER_FILE}" 2>/dev/null)"
if [[ "${rc_c2}" -eq 0 ]] && grep -q '"task_id":""' <<<"${row_c2}"; then
  pass "C2: no --task-id, mission has no H1 -> reserve row task_id is empty (no invented name)"
else
  fail "C2: no --task-id, mission has no H1 -> reserve row task_id is empty (got rc=${rc_c2}, row: ${row_c2}, out: ${out_c2})"
fi

# C3: --task-id PRESENT and mission has an H1 -> reserve row task_id == the --task-id
# (rule 1 wins; guards against this fix hijacking the fanout path, which always binds
# --task-id and must never have it overridden by mission prose).
c3_mission_file="${TMPDIR_ROOT}/c3-mission.md"
cat > "${c3_mission_file}" <<EOF
# N7F-C3-WRONG-NAME — must NOT win over the bound --task-id
body text, dispatch-ledger-task-id c3 $$ $(date +%s 2>/dev/null || echo 0)
EOF
C3_TASK_ID="N7F-C3-BOUND-ID"
out_c3="$(
  CLAUDE_PROJECT_ROOT="${ROOT}" LEADV2_PROJECT_ROOT="${ROOT}" \
  LEADV2_DISPATCH_CACHE_DIR="${CACHE_DIR}" \
  LEADV2_DISPATCH_SUBSESSION_BIN="${FAKE_SUBSESSION}" \
  LEADV2_DISPATCH_ARCHITECT_GATE=0 \
  LEADV2_DISPATCH_E2E_GATE=0 LEADV2_DISPATCH_REVIEW_GATE=0 \
  LEADV2_JOURNAL_BIN=/bin/true \
  LEADV2_ROUTER_V2=0 \
  LEADV2_EXCLUDED_ARMS="__none__" \
  LEADV2_LANE_SHAPE=off \
  "${DISPATCH_SH}" "@${c3_mission_file}" --protected --spawn --kind docs --task-id "${C3_TASK_ID}" 2>&1
)"
rc_c3=$?
row_c3="$(tail -1 "${LEDGER_FILE}" 2>/dev/null)"
if [[ "${rc_c3}" -eq 0 ]] && grep -q "\"task_id\":\"${C3_TASK_ID}\"" <<<"${row_c3}"; then
  pass "C3: --task-id AND mission-H1 both present -> reserve row task_id == bound --task-id (rule 1 wins)"
else
  fail "C3: --task-id AND mission-H1 both present -> reserve row task_id == bound --task-id (got rc=${rc_c3}, row: ${row_c3}, out: ${out_c3})"
fi

# C4/C5 isolate the terminal ledger file the SAME way test-t-core-dispatch-ledger.sh
# does (LEADV2_DISPATCH_TERMINAL_LEDGER_FILE override) rather than re-deriving
# dispatch_terminal_ledger_file()'s CACHE_BASE fallback path here -- that fn tries
# leadv2-state-path.sh FIRST, which (unlike dispatch-code.sh's own simpler
# dispatch_ledger_file()) can resolve to a real path outside this test's sandbox even
# for an isolated tmp repo; the explicit override is what every other write-terminal
# test in this suite family relies on for hermeticity.
TERMINAL_LEDGER_FILE="${TMPDIR_ROOT}/terminal-ledger.jsonl"

# C4: leadv2-dispatch-ledger.sh write-terminal driven directly with a display-name 7th
# arg and an EMPTY founder -- covers the class=product terminal writer (dispatch-
# product-close.sh) without spawning a real close gate. Expect: task_id from the
# display name, founder_task_id stays empty.
C4_SIG8="c4sig888"
C4_NAME="N7F-C4-Display"
LEADV2_DISPATCH_TERMINAL_LEDGER_FILE="${TERMINAL_LEDGER_FILE}" PROJECT_ROOT="${ROOT}" \
  LEADV2_JOURNAL_BIN=/bin/true \
  bash "${LEDGER_SH}" write-terminal "${C4_SIG8}" "" landed test_cause "" "attempt-c4" "${C4_NAME}" >/dev/null 2>&1
row_c4="$(grep -F "\"task_sig\":\"${C4_SIG8}\"" "${TERMINAL_LEDGER_FILE}" 2>/dev/null | tail -1)"
if grep -q "\"task_id\":\"${C4_NAME}\"" <<<"${row_c4}" && grep -q '"founder_task_id":""' <<<"${row_c4}"; then
  pass "C4: write-terminal with empty founder + display-name 7th arg -> task_id from display name, founder_task_id empty"
else
  fail "C4: write-terminal with empty founder + display-name 7th arg (got row: ${row_c4})"
fi

# C5: write-terminal with 6 args (no display name) -> task_id falls back to founder
# (back-compat: a pre-N7F-LANE-NAME caller's output is byte-identical).
C5_SIG8="c5sig888"
C5_FOUNDER="N7F-C5-Founder"
LEADV2_DISPATCH_TERMINAL_LEDGER_FILE="${TERMINAL_LEDGER_FILE}" PROJECT_ROOT="${ROOT}" \
  LEADV2_JOURNAL_BIN=/bin/true \
  bash "${LEDGER_SH}" write-terminal "${C5_SIG8}" "${C5_FOUNDER}" landed test_cause "" "attempt-c5" >/dev/null 2>&1
row_c5="$(grep -F "\"task_sig\":\"${C5_SIG8}\"" "${TERMINAL_LEDGER_FILE}" 2>/dev/null | tail -1)"
if grep -q "\"task_id\":\"${C5_FOUNDER}\"" <<<"${row_c5}"; then
  pass "C5: write-terminal with 6 args (no display name) -> task_id falls back to founder (back-compat)"
else
  fail "C5: write-terminal with 6 args (no display name) -> task_id falls back to founder (got row: ${row_c5})"
fi

# ── N1B-ARM-COOLDOWN-HARDEN F4: identity vs display-label collision ───────────
# Finding 4: a no-`--task-id` mission headed `# OPS-42 — cleanup` used to land
# the H1 name-token "OPS-42" in the identity field, which the status reader then
# resolved against tasks.yaml -> rendered an UNRELATED record's title. After F4
# the label lives in lane_label (rendered verbatim, never looked up), so the row
# shows "OPS-42", not "Totally unrelated record".
RENDER_SH="${SCRIPTS_DIR}/leadv2-status-surface.sh"
F4_REPO="$(printf '%s' "$(basename "${ROOT}")" | tr -cd 'A-Za-z0-9._-')"
# render NOW ~= the reserve moment so the freshly-reserved row is within the
# freshness window (a dead handle at +166 days is age-dropped and never reaches
# resolve_name, which would make this test assert against nothing).
F4_NOW="$(date +%s 2>/dev/null || echo 1800000000)"

# tasks.yaml fixture: an OPS-42 id that is NOT this mission.
F4_TASKS="${TMPDIR_ROOT}/f4-tasks.yaml"
cat > "${F4_TASKS}" <<'YAML'
meta: {}
tasks:
  - id: OPS-42
    title: Totally unrelated record
YAML

# render the worker rows for one isolated ledger; echo the NAME (field 1) of the
# single data row. empty STATE_DIR (no active.yaml) -> reserve row renders as a
# worker row, name = resolve_name(task_id, lane_label, ...).
_f4_render_name() {  # <ledger_dir> <state_dir> <runs_root>
  LEADV2_STATUS_STATE_DIR="$2" \
  LEADV2_STATUS_LEDGER_DIR="$1" \
  LEADV2_STATUS_RUNS_ROOT="$3" \
  LEADV2_STATUS_REPO="${F4_REPO}" \
  LEADV2_STATUS_REPO_ROOT="${ROOT}" \
  LEADV2_STATUS_NOW="${F4_NOW}" \
  LEADV2_STATUS_TASKS_YAML="${F4_TASKS}" \
  bash "${RENDER_SH}" 2>/dev/null | awk '$NF ~ /^[0-9a-f]{6,}$/ {sub(/^ +/,""); sub(/ +(worker|lane) .*/,""); print; exit}'
}

# F4: NO --task-id, mission H1 `# OPS-42 — cleanup` -> renders "OPS-42" (the
# label verbatim), NOT "Totally unrelated record" (the tasks.yaml title).
F4A_CACHE="${TMPDIR_ROOT}/f4a-cache"; F4A_LDIR="${F4A_CACHE}/dispatch-ledger"
F4A_STATE="${TMPDIR_ROOT}/f4a-state"; F4A_RUNS="${TMPDIR_ROOT}/f4a-runs"
mkdir -p "${F4A_LDIR}" "${F4A_STATE}" "${F4A_RUNS}"
# an empty-but-readable active.yaml keeps the renderer on its normal row path
# (a missing active.yaml takes the warn branch and suppresses the worker row).
printf 'meta: {}\nsessions: []\n' > "${F4A_STATE}/active.yaml"
f4a_mission="${TMPDIR_ROOT}/f4a-mission.md"
cat > "${f4a_mission}" <<EOF
# OPS-42 — cleanup, N1B-F4 no-task-id $$ $(date +%s 2>/dev/null || echo 0)
body: display label must not collide with the tasks.yaml OPS-42 identity
EOF
LEADV2_DISPATCH_CACHE_DIR="${F4A_CACHE}" \
  CLAUDE_PROJECT_ROOT="${ROOT}" LEADV2_PROJECT_ROOT="${ROOT}" \
  LEADV2_DISPATCH_SUBSESSION_BIN="${FAKE_SUBSESSION}" \
  LEADV2_DISPATCH_ARCHITECT_GATE=0 \
  LEADV2_DISPATCH_E2E_GATE=0 LEADV2_DISPATCH_REVIEW_GATE=0 \
  LEADV2_JOURNAL_BIN=/bin/true LEADV2_ROUTER_V2=0 \
  LEADV2_EXCLUDED_ARMS="__none__" LEADV2_LANE_SHAPE=off \
  "${DISPATCH_SH}" "@${f4a_mission}" --protected --spawn --kind docs >/dev/null 2>&1
f4a_name="$(_f4_render_name "${F4A_LDIR}" "${F4A_STATE}" "${F4A_RUNS}")"
if [[ "${f4a_name}" == "OPS-42" ]]; then
  pass "F4: no --task-id, mission H1 `# OPS-42 — cleanup` -> renders OPS-42 (not the tasks.yaml title)"
else
  fail "F4: no --task-id collision (got name=[${f4a_name}], want OPS-42)"
fi

# F4b: WITH --task-id OPS-42 + same fixture -> renders the tasks.yaml title
# (the identity lookup is PRESERVED; this guards against the fix over-reaching
# and breaking the bound-identity path).
F4B_CACHE="${TMPDIR_ROOT}/f4b-cache"; F4B_LDIR="${F4B_CACHE}/dispatch-ledger"
F4B_STATE="${TMPDIR_ROOT}/f4b-state"; F4B_RUNS="${TMPDIR_ROOT}/f4b-runs"
mkdir -p "${F4B_LDIR}" "${F4B_STATE}" "${F4B_RUNS}"
printf 'meta: {}\nsessions: []\n' > "${F4B_STATE}/active.yaml"
f4b_mission="${TMPDIR_ROOT}/f4b-mission.md"
cat > "${f4b_mission}" <<EOF
# OPS-42 — cleanup, N1B-F4b with-task-id $$ $(date +%s 2>/dev/null || echo 0)
body: bound --task-id OPS-42 must still resolve via tasks.yaml
EOF
LEADV2_DISPATCH_CACHE_DIR="${F4B_CACHE}" \
  CLAUDE_PROJECT_ROOT="${ROOT}" LEADV2_PROJECT_ROOT="${ROOT}" \
  LEADV2_DISPATCH_SUBSESSION_BIN="${FAKE_SUBSESSION}" \
  LEADV2_DISPATCH_ARCHITECT_GATE=0 \
  LEADV2_DISPATCH_E2E_GATE=0 LEADV2_DISPATCH_REVIEW_GATE=0 \
  LEADV2_JOURNAL_BIN=/bin/true LEADV2_ROUTER_V2=0 \
  LEADV2_EXCLUDED_ARMS="__none__" LEADV2_LANE_SHAPE=off \
  "${DISPATCH_SH}" "@${f4b_mission}" --protected --spawn --kind docs --task-id OPS-42 >/dev/null 2>&1
f4b_name="$(_f4_render_name "${F4B_LDIR}" "${F4B_STATE}" "${F4B_RUNS}")"
if [[ "${f4b_name}" == "Totally unrelated record" ]]; then
  pass "F4b: --task-id OPS-42 -> renders the tasks.yaml title (identity lookup preserved)"
else
  fail "F4b: identity lookup (got name=[${f4b_name}], want 'Totally unrelated record')"
fi

printf '[TEST] === %s passed, %s failed ===\n' "${PASS}" "${FAIL}"
[[ "${FAIL}" -eq 0 ]]

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# tests/test-dispatch-terminal-preflight-refusal.sh — DISPATCH-TERMINAL-PREFLIGHT-01
#
# THE BUG: re-dispatching a mission whose task-sig (sig8) already has a TRUE terminal
# (landed|dead) recorded in the terminal ledger (leadv2-dispatch-ledger.sh) sailed
# straight through dispatch-code.sh's cmd_resolve -- reservation, spawn, the works --
# because cmd_resolve never consulted the terminal ledger at all (only the SEPARATE
# reservation ledger, which frees up once liveness proves the earlier worker dead). The
# re-dispatch's own outcome write then lost the terminal ledger's write-once race
# (dispatch_terminal_dedup, rc treated as a successful no-op by design) and the whole
# process exited 0 with no worker output, no diff, no error logged anywhere but the
# journal -- indistinguishable from the outside from "ran and did nothing" (2026-08-07
# repro, dispatch-f41dfb1b mission).
#
# THIS TEST drives the REAL dispatch-code.sh (never a hand-reimplemented copy of the
# preflight logic), same hermetic-fixture discipline as
# test-dispatch-ledger-task-id.sh / test-leadv2-dispatch-outcome-ledger.sh.
#
# Run: bash plugins/leadv2/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-terminal-preflight-refusal.sh

set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
SCRIPTS_DIR="$(cd "${SCRIPT_DIR}/.." && pwd)"
DISPATCH_SH="${SCRIPTS_DIR}/leadv2-dispatch-code.sh"
LEDGER_SH="${SCRIPTS_DIR}/leadv2-dispatch-ledger.sh"
source "${SCRIPTS_DIR}/leadv2-temp.sh"

PASS=0; FAIL=0
pass() { PASS=$((PASS + 1)); printf '[TEST] PASS: %s\n' "$1"; }
fail() { FAIL=$((FAIL + 1)); printf '[TEST] FAIL: %s\n' "$1"; }

if bash -n "${DISPATCH_SH}" 2>/dev/null; then
  pass "bash -n leadv2-dispatch-code.sh"
else
  fail "bash -n leadv2-dispatch-code.sh"
fi
if bash -n "${LEDGER_SH}" 2>/dev/null; then
  pass "bash -n leadv2-dispatch-ledger.sh"
else
  fail "bash -n leadv2-dispatch-ledger.sh"
fi
if bash -n "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}" 2>/dev/null; then
  pass "bash -n $(basename "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")"
else
  fail "bash -n $(basename "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")"
fi

RUN_ID="dispatch-terminal-preflight-$$-$(date +%s 2>/dev/null || echo 0)"
TMPDIR_ROOT="$(lv2_mktemp_dir "${RUN_ID}")"
ROOT="${TMPDIR_ROOT}/repo"
CACHE_DIR="${TMPDIR_ROOT}/cache"
TERMINAL_LEDGER_FILE="${TMPDIR_ROOT}/terminal-ledger.jsonl"
FAKE_SUBSESSION="${TMPDIR_ROOT}/fake-claude-subsession.sh"
SPAWN_MARKER="${TMPDIR_ROOT}/spawn-marker"
trap 'rm -rf "$TMPDIR_ROOT"' EXIT

mkdir -p "${ROOT}/.claude/ref" "${ROOT}/docs/leadv2/.bus-offsets" "${ROOT}/platform"
( cd "${ROOT}" && git init -q && git config user.email test@example.com && git config user.name test \
  && printf 'seed\n' > seed.txt && git add seed.txt && git commit -qm seed )

cat > "${ROOT}/.claude/ref/leadv2-routing.yaml" <<'YAML'
router:
  glm_policy:
    sonnet_exceptions:
      - id: safety_gate_publish_payments
    opus_only_mission_kinds: []
    codex_fitting_mission_kinds: []
    codex_default_tier: standard
YAML

# Same fake launcher shape as the other dispatch-code tests: spawns a real, short-lived
# OS process and prints its PID in the exact shape spawn_worker's sonnet-arm parser
# expects. Also drops a marker file so a refused dispatch (which must NEVER reach the
# launcher) is provably distinguishable from one that did.
cat > "${FAKE_SUBSESSION}" <<EOF
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -uo pipefail
printf 'spawned\n' >> "${SPAWN_MARKER}"
nohup sleep 0.3 >/dev/null 2>&1 &
pid=\$!
disown
printf 'PID=%s LABEL=fake-lane SESSION_ID=fake-session\n' "\${pid}"
exit 0
EOF
chmod +x "${FAKE_SUBSESSION}"

_run_dispatch() {  # <mission-text>
  CLAUDE_PROJECT_ROOT="${ROOT}" LEADV2_PROJECT_ROOT="${ROOT}" \
  LEADV2_DISPATCH_CACHE_DIR="${CACHE_DIR}" \
  LEADV2_DISPATCH_SUBSESSION_BIN="${FAKE_SUBSESSION}" \
  LEADV2_DISPATCH_ARCHITECT_GATE=0 \
  LEADV2_DISPATCH_E2E_GATE=0 LEADV2_DISPATCH_REVIEW_GATE=0 \
  LEADV2_JOURNAL_BIN=/bin/true \
  LEADV2_ROUTER_V2=0 \
  LEADV2_EXCLUDED_ARMS="__none__" \

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# tests/test-dispatch-terminal-preflight-refusal.sh — DISPATCH-TERMINAL-PREFLIGHT-01
#
# THE BUG: re-dispatching a mission whose task-sig (sig8) already has a TRUE terminal
# (landed|dead) recorded in the terminal ledger (leadv2-dispatch-ledger.sh) sailed
# straight through dispatch-code.sh's cmd_resolve -- reservation, spawn, the works --
# because cmd_resolve never consulted the terminal ledger at all (only the SEPARATE
# reservation ledger, which frees up once liveness proves the earlier worker dead). The
# re-dispatch's own outcome write then lost the terminal ledger's write-once race
# (dispatch_terminal_dedup, rc treated as a successful no-op by design) and the whole
# process exited 0 with no worker output, no diff, no error logged anywhere but the
# journal -- indistinguishable from the outside from "ran and did nothing" (2026-08-07
# repro, dispatch-f41dfb1b mission).
#
# THIS TEST drives the REAL dispatch-code.sh (never a hand-reimplemented copy of the
# preflight logic), same hermetic-fixture discipline as
# test-dispatch-ledger-task-id.sh / test-leadv2-dispatch-outcome-ledger.sh.
#
# Run: bash plugins/leadv2/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-terminal-preflight-refusal.sh

set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
SCRIPTS_DIR="$(cd "${SCRIPT_DIR}/.." && pwd)"
DISPATCH_SH="${SCRIPTS_DIR}/leadv2-dispatch-code.sh"
LEDGER_SH="${SCRIPTS_DIR}/leadv2-dispatch-ledger.sh"
source "${SCRIPTS_DIR}/leadv2-temp.sh"

PASS=0; FAIL=0
pass() { PASS=$((PASS + 1)); printf '[TEST] PASS: %s\n' "$1"; }
fail() { FAIL=$((FAIL + 1)); printf '[TEST] FAIL: %s\n' "$1"; }

if bash -n "${DISPATCH_SH}" 2>/dev/null; then
  pass "bash -n leadv2-dispatch-code.sh"
else
  fail "bash -n leadv2-dispatch-code.sh"
fi
if bash -n "${LEDGER_SH}" 2>/dev/null; then
  pass "bash -n leadv2-dispatch-ledger.sh"
else
  fail "bash -n leadv2-dispatch-ledger.sh"
fi
if bash -n "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}" 2>/dev/null; then
  pass "bash -n $(basename "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")"
else
  fail "bash -n $(basename "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")"
fi

RUN_ID="dispatch-terminal-preflight-$$-$(date +%s 2>/dev/null || echo 0)"
TMPDIR_ROOT="$(lv2_mktemp_dir "${RUN_ID}")"
ROOT="${TMPDIR_ROOT}/repo"
CACHE_DIR="${TMPDIR_ROOT}/cache"
TERMINAL_LEDGER_FILE="${TMPDIR_ROOT}/terminal-ledger.jsonl"
FAKE_SUBSESSION="${TMPDIR_ROOT}/fake-claude-subsession.sh"
SPAWN_MARKER="${TMPDIR_ROOT}/spawn-marker"
trap 'rm -rf "$TMPDIR_ROOT"' EXIT

mkdir -p "${ROOT}/.claude/ref" "${ROOT}/docs/leadv2/.bus-offsets" "${ROOT}/platform"
( cd "${ROOT}" && git init -q && git config user.email test@example.com && git config user.name test \

cat > "${ROOT}/.claude/ref/leadv2-routing.yaml" <<'YAML'
router:

# Same fake launcher shape as the other dispatch-code tests: spawns a real, short-lived

disown

_run_dispatch() {  # <mission-text>

# Re-dispatching a lane whose terminal is already recorded now refuses loudly

## Root cause

`leadv2-dispatch-code.sh`'s `cmd_resolve` (the sole entrypoint for a dispatch) guards
against an in-flight duplicate via the **reservation** ledger (`dispatch_reserve` /
`_dispatch_sig_blocked`, pending/confirmed rows, freed once liveness proves the worker
dead) but never once consulted the **separate** terminal ledger
(`leadv2-dispatch-ledger.sh`'s `dispatch_terminal_exists`, write-once landed|dead rows).
So a re-dispatch of a sig8 whose earlier attempt already recorded `dead` (crashed,
timed out, whatever) sailed straight through reserve → confirm → spawn → the worker's
own outcome write, lost the terminal ledger's write-once race on that write (`dedup is a
SUCCESSFUL no-op, not a caller error`, by design), and exited 0 with no worker output, no
diff, no error anywhere but the journal. From the outside this is indistinguishable from
"a lane ran and changed nothing" — the exact 2026-08-07 repro in the mission
(`dispatch_terminal_dedup task=466b8998 attempted=dead reason=terminal_already_recorded`
x2, rc=0).

## What changed

**Chosen design: refuse loudly, never re-open.** The write-once terminal ledger's own
doc comments state the design principle already ("`--force` is, by design, never
permitted for dedup" — leadv2-dispatch-code.sh:174, re the reservation ledger's
CONFIRMED_TTL block). Applying the identical principle to the terminal ledger — no
bypass flag, ever — is consistent with that existing convention and lower-risk than
introducing a re-open path that would let an operator resurrect a write-once `dead`/
`landed` row the ledger's whole design treats as final. A refusal is also exactly the
shape `_resolve_pinned_placement` already uses at this same point in `cmd_resolve` (exit
5 on placement refusal) — this fix is `_resolve_pinned_placement`'s sibling, not a new
pattern.

1. **`plugins/leadv2/scripts/leadv2-dispatch-ledger.sh`**
   - New `dispatch_terminal_show(sig8)`: read-only detail sitting directly behind the
     existing `dispatch_terminal_exists()` (same rc0/rc1 contract — refused/parked never
     count). On rc0 it prints `terminal=<x> cause=<y> ts=<z>` so a caller can build a
     refusal message that *names* what already happened, not just that something did.
   - New `show <sig8>` CLI subcommand wiring `dispatch_terminal_show` (mirrors the
     existing `exists <sig8>` subcommand). Usage text updated.

2. **`plugins/leadv2/scripts/leadv2-dispatch-code.sh`**
   - `cmd_resolve`: immediately after `sig8` is computed and validated (right before
     `_resolve_pinned_placement`, i.e. before ANY reservation/spawn — same ordering
     `_resolve_pinned_placement`'s own doc comment already documents), calls
     `leadv2-dispatch-ledger.sh show <sig8>` (gated on the existing `TERMINAL_LEDGER=1`
     flag, same as every other terminal-ledger touchpoint in this file). If a TRUE
     terminal (landed|dead) exists:
     - journals `dispatch_refused_terminal_exists task=<sig8> terminal=<x> cause=<y>
       ts=<z>` via the existing `emit` helper,
     - prints one stderr line naming the prior terminal/cause and explicitly stating
       there is no bypass,
     - `exit 6`.
   - Usage doc's exit-code list extended with `6 terminal already recorded`.
   - A retryable prior outcome (refused|parked) is **not** blocked — `dispatch_terminal_show`
     inherits `dispatch_terminal_exists`'s existing refused/parked-is-not-a-terminal
     semantics, so a later genuine retry attempt still records its own real landed/dead
     outcome, exactly as it does today (Case 3 in the test below proves this).
   - The diff-hash dedup ("your new work produced an identical diff", `review_gate
     status=dedup`) is a completely separate check in `leadv2-review-run.sh` /
     `leadv2-dispatch-product-close.sh` — untouched. The mission's two failure modes
     ("you re-ran an already-finished task" vs "your new work happened to produce the
     same diff") were already distinguishable in the codebase; the bug was only that the
     FIRST one produced no signal at all. My stderr message for the terminal refusal
     explicitly calls out that a same-diff outcome is a separate fact checked elsewhere.

Neither task-signature derivation (`compute_sig`) nor the reservation ledger's own
blocking logic was touched — both hard limits respected.

## Tests

New suite: `plugins/leadv2/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-terminal-preflight-refusal.sh`.
Drives the REAL `leadv2-dispatch-code.sh` (never a hand-reimplemented copy), same
hermetic-fixture discipline as `test-dispatch-ledger-task-id.sh`.

- **C1** (the bug): pre-seed the terminal ledger with a `dead` row for a sig8, then
  re-dispatch the identical mission text. Asserts: exit non-zero, refusal message names
  `terminal=dead cause=worker_timeout`, and the fake worker launcher is **never invoked**
  (a marker file the launcher writes is absent).
- **C2** (regression guard): a fresh mission with no prior terminal still dispatches
  (exit 0, launcher invoked) — same shape as before the fix.
- **C3** (retryable rows unaffected): a sig8 whose only prior row is `refused` (not a
  TRUE terminal) is **not** blocked — re-dispatch proceeds and reaches the launcher,
  preserving `dispatch_terminal_exists`'s existing "a later attempt must still be able to
  record its real outcome" semantics.

### RED, against the untouched pre-fix files (git checkout -- the two source files, same
tree, same test, nothing about the test itself changed)

```

[TEST] FAIL: C1: refusal message names the prior terminal and cause (got out: [leadv2-dispatch-code] dispatch_classified task=33217829 class=non_product reason=explicit_kind_docs kind=docs
[leadv2-dispatch-code] phase_precondition_warn task=33217829 class=Standard missing=plan,gate1,build,test,review,live_verify,close mode=warn
[leadv2-dispatch-code] arm_resolved job=build arm=sonnet reason=safety_gate_publish_payments
[leadv2-dispatch-code] candidate_chain task=33217829 arms=sonnet
[leadv2-dispatch-code] worker_spawned by=router model=sonnet task=33217829 attempt=33217829-1786098139-42090 handle=PID=42761 LABEL=fake-lane SESSION_ID=fake-session
...
route_resolved by=router router=v1 model=sonnet task=33217829 rule=safety_gate_publish_payments reason=sonnet_exception
[leadv2-dispatch-code] lane_worktree_left task=33217829 founder_task= path=/Users/kostiantyn.vlasenko/Projects/leadv2/.claude/worktrees/f41dfb1b)

```
(run aborted before C2/C3 in this capture — the worker spawn it should never have
reached hangs the harness verifying process death; the three FAILs above are the
load-bearing proof: exit 0, no refusal message, worker actually spawned)

### GREEN, with the fix applied

```

[TEST] PASS: C3: a retryable prior outcome (refused) does not block re-dispatch
[TEST] === 9 passed, 0 failed ===
```
Reproduced clean on 3 separate runs after the fix (flakiness note below).

## Proof: one real re-dispatch, journal lines verbatim

```

[leadv2-dispatch-code] REFUSE dispatch: task=e9a0c599 already has a recorded terminal (terminal=dead cause=worker_timeout ts=2026-08-07T10:32:21Z) -- this mission signature already reached a final outcome; re-dispatching it is a no-op by design (write-once terminal ledger, same "never permitted for dedup" rule the reservation ledger uses). If this re-dispatch produced a genuinely new diff, that is a SEPARATE fact from this refusal -- diffs are compared by the review-ledger diff-hash dedup, not here. If new work is actually needed, change the mission text (a different sig8 is a fresh task); there is no bypass flag for this refusal by design.
```

- `tests/test-dispatch-ledger-task-id.sh` — 9/14 fail (`row: ` empty on C2/C3, `name=[]`

- The reservation ledger (`dispatch_reserve`, pending/confirmed rows) — untouched; this

- No re-open/bypass flag was added (see "Chosen design" above) — an operator who

## Root cause

`leadv2-dispatch-code.sh`'s `cmd_resolve` (the sole entrypoint for a dispatch) guards
against an in-flight duplicate via the **reservation** ledger (`dispatch_reserve` /
`_dispatch_sig_blocked`, pending/confirmed rows, freed once liveness proves the worker
dead) but never once consulted the **separate** terminal ledger
(`leadv2-dispatch-ledger.sh`'s `dispatch_terminal_exists`, write-once landed|dead rows).
So a re-dispatch of a sig8 whose earlier attempt already recorded `dead` (crashed,
timed out, whatever) sailed straight through reserve → confirm → spawn → the worker's
own outcome write, lost the terminal ledger's write-once race on that write (`dedup is a
SUCCESSFUL no-op, not a caller error`, by design), and exited 0 with no worker output, no
diff, no error anywhere but the journal. From the outside this is indistinguishable from
"a lane ran and changed nothing" — the exact 2026-08-07 repro in the mission
(`dispatch_terminal_dedup task=466b8998 attempted=dead reason=terminal_already_recorded`
x2, rc=0).

## What changed

**Chosen design: refuse loudly, never re-open.** The write-once terminal ledger's own
doc comments state the design principle already ("`--force` is, by design, never
permitted for dedup" — leadv2-dispatch-code.sh:174, re the reservation ledger's
CONFIRMED_TTL block). Applying the identical principle to the terminal ledger — no
bypass flag, ever — is consistent with that existing convention and lower-risk than
introducing a re-open path that would let an operator resurrect a write-once `dead`/
`landed` row the ledger's whole design treats as final. A refusal is also exactly the
shape `_resolve_pinned_placement` already uses at this same point in `cmd_resolve` (exit
5 on placement refusal) — this fix is `_resolve_pinned_placement`'s sibling, not a new
pattern.

1. **`plugins/leadv2/scripts/leadv2-dispatch-ledger.sh`**
   - New `dispatch_terminal_show(sig8)`: read-only detail sitting directly behind the
     existing `dispatch_terminal_exists()` (same rc0/rc1 contract — refused/parked never
     count). On rc0 it prints `terminal=<x> cause=<y> ts=<z>` so a caller can build a
     refusal message that *names* what already happened, not just that something did.
   - New `show <sig8>` CLI subcommand wiring `dispatch_terminal_show` (mirrors the
     existing `exists <sig8>` subcommand). Usage text updated.

2. **`plugins/leadv2/scripts/leadv2-dispatch-code.sh`**
   - `cmd_resolve`: immediately after `sig8` is computed and validated (right before
     `_resolve_pinned_placement`, i.e. before ANY reservation/spawn — same ordering
     `_resolve_pinned_placement`'s own doc comment already documents), calls
     `leadv2-dispatch-ledger.sh show <sig8>` (gated on the existing `TERMINAL_LEDGER=1`
     flag, same as every other terminal-ledger touchpoint in this file). If a TRUE
     terminal (landed|dead) exists:
     - journals `dispatch_refused_terminal_exists task=<sig8> terminal=<x> cause=<y>
       ts=<z>` via the existing `emit` helper,
     - prints one stderr line naming the prior terminal/cause and explicitly stating
       there is no bypass,
     - `exit 6`.
   - Usage doc's exit-code list extended with `6 terminal already recorded`.
   - A retryable prior outcome (refused|parked) is **not** blocked — `dispatch_terminal_show`
     inherits `dispatch_terminal_exists`'s existing refused/parked-is-not-a-terminal
     semantics, so a later genuine retry attempt still records its own real landed/dead
     outcome, exactly as it does today (Case 3 in the test below proves this).
   - The diff-hash dedup ("your new work produced an identical diff", `review_gate
     status=dedup`) is a completely separate check in `leadv2-review-run.sh` /
     `leadv2-dispatch-product-close.sh` — untouched. The mission's two failure modes
     ("you re-ran an already-finished task" vs "your new work happened to produce the
     same diff") were already distinguishable in the codebase; the bug was only that the
     FIRST one produced no signal at all. My stderr message for the terminal refusal
     explicitly calls out that a same-diff outcome is a separate fact checked elsewhere.

Neither task-signature derivation (`compute_sig`) nor the reservation ledger's own
blocking logic was touched — both hard limits respected.

## Tests

New suite: `plugins/leadv2/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-terminal-preflight-refusal.sh`.
Drives the REAL `leadv2-dispatch-code.sh` (never a hand-reimplemented copy), same
hermetic-fixture discipline as `test-dispatch-ledger-task-id.sh`.

- **C1** (the bug): pre-seed the terminal ledger with a `dead` row for a sig8, then
  re-dispatch the identical mission text. Asserts: exit non-zero, refusal message names
  `terminal=dead cause=worker_timeout`, and the fake worker launcher is **never invoked**
  (a marker file the launcher writes is absent).
- **C2** (regression guard): a fresh mission with no prior terminal still dispatches
  (exit 0, launcher invoked) — same shape as before the fix.
- **C3** (retryable rows unaffected): a sig8 whose only prior row is `refused` (not a
  TRUE terminal) is **not** blocked — re-dispatch proceeds and reaches the launcher,
  preserving `dispatch_terminal_exists`'s existing "a later attempt must still be able to
  record its real outcome" semantics.

Reproduced clean on 3 separate runs after the fix (flakiness note below).

## Proof: one real re-dispatch, journal lines verbatim

```
sig8=e9a0c599
--- prior terminal recorded, now re-dispatching the SAME mission ---
[leadv2-dispatch-code] dispatch_refused_terminal_exists task=e9a0c599 terminal=dead cause=worker_timeout ts=2026-08-07T10:32:21Z
[leadv2-dispatch-code] REFUSE dispatch: task=e9a0c599 already has a recorded terminal (terminal=dead cause=worker_timeout ts=2026-08-07T10:32:21Z) -- this mission signature already reached a final outcome; re-dispatching it is a no-op by design (write-once terminal ledger, same "never permitted for dedup" rule the reservation ledger uses). If this re-dispatch produced a genuinely new diff, that is a SEPARATE fact from this refusal -- diffs are compared by the review-ledger diff-hash dedup, not here. If new work is actually needed, change the mission text (a different sig8 is a fresh task); there is no bypass flag for this refusal by design.
RC=6
```

## Verified: three suites red on untouched main are NOT mine (checked both before and after applying the fix, byte-identical failure on both)

- `tests/test-dispatch-ledger-task-id.sh` — 9/14 fail (`row: ` empty on C2/C3, `name=[]`
  on F4/F4b). Confirmed identical failure with the fix applied AND with the two source
  files reverted to untouched `main` — environment-sensitive (this test's own doc header
  hints at similar prior fragility with lane-name rendering), not caused by this change.
- `tests/test-dispatch-ledger-partial-close.sh` — 8/8 fail, all `setup — first dispatch
  or process-death wait failed (rc=3)`. Same: confirmed identical on untouched `main`.
- `run-core-offline.sh` — per the mission's own hard-limits section, already known red on
  main (rc=124 at 600s), not investigated further here.

I did not touch any of these three suites or their fixtures.

## What I deliberately left alone

- The reservation ledger (`dispatch_reserve`, pending/confirmed rows) — untouched; this
  fix adds a check BEFORE it runs, never modifies its own logic.
- No re-open/bypass flag was added (see "Chosen design" above) — an operator who
  genuinely needs new work done must change the mission text (a new sig8 is, by
  definition, a fresh task; this is explicit in the refusal message).
- `run_id`/sig8 derivation (`compute_sig`) — untouched, per hard limits.
- Test-fixture launcher's `sleep` duration in my own new test bumped from the
  `0.3`s other dispatch-code tests use to `2`s after observing one flaky `rc=4
  spawn(sonnet)... not_live` failure on C2 under heavy concurrent background-process
  load in this session (same fake-subsession `nohup sleep N & disown; kill -0` liveness
  race every dispatch-code test in this family shares) — not a defect in the fix itself,
  reproduced clean 3/3 after the bump.
